evidence_found: A draft software policy sits in the shared drive (demo-estate/policy-draft.md). No approval date, no named owner, nobody could say if it is followed.
One application list (demo-estate/apps.csv) holds 60 applications, each with a cost, a user count, and a checked-on date of 2026-09-01. The IT team refreshes it every quarter.
Asked procurement, finance, and two team leads for a request form or approval path. Nobody could produce one.
The IT manager says laptops are reviewed at refresh time. Nothing is written down, and no review dates appear in any file.
A license list (demo-estate/licenses.csv) records entitlements and expiry dates. A monthly count of licenses expiring in 90 days is kept, but no renewal has changed because of it.
Annual cost and user count sit beside every application in demo-estate/apps.csv, and the finance partner reviews the list each quarter.
Every application carries a data-sensitivity rating, and the six AI systems are listed with an owner (demo-estate/ai-systems.csv). A review is run before new tools are approved.
A retirement checklist was copied into the shared drive last year. No completed sign-off form can be found for any retirement.
A one-page report with four measures goes to the CIO each month, each with a target and a stated response. The last two reports led to a change in the renewal calendar.
Asked three application owners what they had been told about their duties. None could name one.
